title: What Israel’s Election Won't Change
gist: Teaser of Aluf Benn's piece arguing Israel's October 27 election will not change the new security consensus; available text recounts Netanyahu's aggressive record under nearly two decades of rule.

insights.claim: Israelis vote on October 27 with much of the world rooting for Benjamin Netanyahu's defeat, but the article argues the election will not change the country's new security consensus.
insights.speaker: Aluf Benn
insights.so_what: A change of leader may not shift Israeli regional security policy, which tempers geopolitical risk repricing on an election outcome.
insights.locator: When Israelis go to the polls on October 27

insights.claim: Under Netanyahu's nearly two decades of rule Israel has abandoned any pretense of supporting a two-state solution and begun building hundreds of new settlements in the West Bank.
insights.speaker: Aluf Benn
insights.so_what: Settlement expansion entrenches the conflict and constrains any diplomatic normalization path.
insights.locator: Under his nearly two decades of rule

insights.claim: Since Hamas's October 7, 2023 attack Israel has laid waste to Gaza, occupied parts of Lebanon and Syria, and launched war against Iran.
insights.speaker: Aluf Benn
insights.so_what: Multi-front military posture sustains regional risk across energy and shipping.

insights.claim: Israel's democratic institutions have faced endless attacks from Netanyahu and his allies.
insights.speaker: Aluf Benn
insights.so_what: Institutional erosion is a political-risk factor for Israeli assets.
